test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: general
question: The radius of the base of a cylindrical tank is 4 m. If three times the sum of the areas of its two circular faces is twice the area of its curved surface, then the capacity (in kilolitres) of the tank is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the condition: 3 × (2 × Area of circle) = 2 × (Curved Surface Area)

3 × (2πr²) = 2 × (2πrh)

⇒ 6r = 4h → h = 1.5r

⇒ h = 1.5 × 4 = 6 m

⇒ Volume = π × r² × h = π × 4² × 6 = 96π m³

Since 1 m³ = 1 kilolitre (kL), Capacity = 96π kL.

**∴ The correct answer is 96 π kL.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Radius (r) = 4 m

Formula Used: Area of circular face = πr²; Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh; Volume = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fca0b110e0c38cb9bdddf6cd9b03a2afe657b5ca20aee3bec4a1b647a250fb8e.png] 

⇒ Let the height of the tank be h.

⇒ Sum of areas of two circular faces = 2 × πr²

⇒ According to question: 3 × (2πr²) = 2 × (2πrh)

⇒ 6πr² = 4πrh

⇒ 6 × 4² = 4 × 4 × h

⇒ 6 × 16 = 16 × h

⇒ h = 6 m

⇒ Capacity = Volume = πr²h

⇒ Capacity = π × (4)² × 6

⇒ Capacity = π × 16 × 6 = 96π m³

⇒ Since 1 m³ = 1000 Litres = 1 kL

⇒ Capacity = 96π kL

**∴ The correct answer is 96 π kL.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and both top and bottom bases: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(r + h).

Volume and Capacity Units

1 cubic meter (m³) is equivalent to 1000 liters, which is defined as 1 kilolitre (kL). Thus, Volume in m³ = Capacity in kL.

Right Circular Cylinder

A cylinder where the axis joining the centers of the circular bases is perpendicular to the planes of the bases.</p
